speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly what happens during these episodes of unresponsiveness, and how long they last?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: The muddy taste you felt before the episodes is a very specific warning sign, often called an aura. Can you describe the hand gestures your brother saw, and do you notice if anything seems to trigger these episodes?

speaker: Doctor
text: Did your brother see you picking at your clothes or rubbing your hands, and do these episodes happen more often when you are tired or stressed? Have you had any fever or recent head injury?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history. No prior seizures or neurological evaluations. Social history: Enrolled in second grade. Lives with parents and one sibling. No reported use of medications or exposure to toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do these episodes tend to occur when you are sleeping or right after you wake up? Also, have you noticed any stiffening of your limbs or loss of bladder control during these events?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, headache, visual or auditory disturbances, weakness, or other systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do these episodes happen while you are awake, and do you or your family notice any tongue biting or drooling during the event? Given the specific aura and post-episode confusion, I would like to order an EEG to check for abnormal brain activity. REQUEST TEST: EEG.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electroencephalogram: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The EEG confirms abnormal electrical activity in your temporal lobes, which aligns with the aura and confusion you described. DIAGNOSIS READY: Temporal Lobe Epilepsy.
